headline: The town advanced a designer for the Neary School study, closed hearings on a 32-unit 40B, and opted out of school choice.
synopsis: The Elementary School Building Committee interviewed finalists and voted to advance Tappe Architects into contract negotiations for the Neary School feasibility study. In land use, the Zoning Board of Appeals closed the public hearing for a 32-unit Chapter 40B townhome proposal at 250 Turnpike Road, while the Planning Board reviewed zoning compliance problems at commercial sites along Route 9. The Regional School Committee voted unanimously to withdraw from state School Choice for the 2026-2027 school year to protect local class size limits. Other municipal bodies reviewed park improvement designs, analyzed resident feedback showing reduced satisfaction with town web tools, and approved a scope for a townwide compensation study.

highlights.title: Tappe Architects selected for Neary School study negotiations
highlights.why: The Elementary School Building Committee voted unanimously to advance Tappe Architects to contract negotiations for the Neary Elementary School feasibility study. The firm will assess renovation, repair, and deferred maintenance options.

highlights.title: Hearing closed on 250 Turnpike Road Chapter 40B project
highlights.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals concluded public testimony on a 32-unit rental townhome proposal and will draft conditions and deliberate in May. The town is currently three units away from reaching the 10 percent subsidized housing safe harbor threshold.

highlights.title: Regional school district withdraws from School Choice
highlights.why: The Regional School Committee voted unanimously to opt out of the state School Choice program for the 2026-2027 school year. Officials cited class size caps and a gap between the five thousand dollar state reimbursement and Algonquin per-pupil operating costs.

highlights.title: Planning Board raises zoning compliance concerns at 200 Turnpike Road
highlights.why: Board members reviewed reports that building permits and certificates of occupancy were issued without required planning board approvals or certified as-built plans. The board plans a joint workshop with town administration and the building commissioner on enforcement.

highlights.title: Fay Memorial Park redesign concepts reviewed ahead of public forum
highlights.why: The Recreation Commission reviewed updated plans that reduce the proposed splash pad footprint and adjust its location near existing park amenities. Commissioners are preparing surveys and materials ahead of a public forum scheduled for May 20.

highlights.title: Survey data shows decline in satisfaction with town web services
highlights.why: Resident feedback presented to the Municipal Technology Committee showed overall satisfaction with town technology fell in 2025, driven by difficulties with website navigation and digital forms. Email remains the preferred contact method for 79 percent of respondents.
